stages.name: Staged
stages.instructions:
Prepare the release this card names, so the checks stage has something concrete to examine.

Work on the card's own branch, so the next stage can find what you produced even if it runs on
another machine. Stages may share a host today; that is luck, not design, and it fails silently
the day a station moves.

  directory  ./.release/<cardId>/ inside the directory you start in.
  branch     release/<cardId>.
  repository the card's target, cloned by its ordinary GitHub URL — this host rewrites
             forge-primary repositories to forge automatically, and your station key is what
             authenticates the push.

Push what you prepared. An artifact that exists only on the machine you built it on is not staged,
it is stranded, and the next stage will be checking nothing.

Complete with a `version` in your handoff — the exact tag or identifier you prepared, as a reader
would type it — and attach the forge commit as a reference. The reference is what proves the work
left this station; without it, "staged" is a word rather than a fact. This board exists because
that distinction has been got wrong before.

stages.name: Checks
stages.instructions:
Run the release checks against what the previous stage staged, and report what they said.

Start from the staged branch and the `version` in the handoff — not from `main`, and not from a
fresh build of your own. Checking something other than the artifact that will ship is the one
failure this stage cannot recover from, because it produces a confident pass about the wrong thing.

Run every check the card's spec names. If the spec names none, say so in your verdict rather than
inventing a set — a check nobody asked for passing tells a reader nothing about what was required.

Complete with a `verdict` in your handoff: `pass` or `fail`, the checks you ran, and their output
or a pointer to it.

**A failing check is a successful stage.** Report `fail` with the detail and let the go/no-go gate
decide; do not fix the problem yourself. Fixing it here means the thing that ships was never
checked in the state it ships in, which is the same defect as checking the wrong artifact.
